rationale:
THE CONTROL for module-leaf-declaration-file.d (VERIFY_TS10). Leaf identity is `basename` minus the LAST extension: `dotfile-stem.module.config.ts` publishes `dotfile-stem.module.config`. Only a DECLARATION file's `.d` is part of the extension rather than of the name. The NAME is the assertion and it had to be chosen to make the two rules distinguishable — the first version of this fixture was `module-leaf-dotfile-stem.ts`, whose only dots belong to the extension, so a mutant cutting at the FIRST dot returned the identical string and this control passed under it (measured: the mutant run reported 93 pass / 0 fail with the control still green). A control that cannot tell the two rules apart is not a control.

2026-11-17: the SOURCE of a module-level row is now the file-level sentinel `(file)` (JS-twin parity; `FILE_LEVEL_SOURCE`), so the leaf is no longer the source spelling — the assertion moved WITH the leaf, to `metadata.scopeName`, and the rows carry `metadata.fileLevel: true`. The leaf rule is unchanged and still load-bearing: the forbid rows below are the over-stripped spelling (cutting at the FIRST dot), now on scopeName where that spelling would live.

expectRelationships.note: the leaf keeps every interior dot: basename minus the LAST extension — asserted on metadata.scopeName, where the module leaf now lives, and the source is the file-level sentinel
CONTROL: the call edge names the module too and is affected the same way

forbidRelationships.note: over-stripping: cutting at the FIRST dot would name the module `dotfile-stem` — forbidden on the scopeName half, since that is where the leaf lives now
